div.div:
aequĭpărābĭlis (better, aequipĕr- ), e, adj. aequiparo,
I.that may be compared, comparable (perh only in Plaut.); with dat.: diis aequiperabile, Curc. 1, 3, 11.—With cum, Trin. 2, 4, 65 (also in Non. 304).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
